tone_statements.quote: 2.3.1 Tones Three general tones are identified in Hlersu , which are namely the high level , the mid - level , and the low falling . The last two can be further classified into the lax and tense subcategories , i.e. the lax mid - level tone , the lax low falling tone , the tense mid - level tone , and the tense low falling tone . Tense tones are generally pronounced with greater pitches than lax ones . See Table 2-4 for exemplary words with distinctive tones . ... ( 2 ) The high falling tone of 51 is marked in some exemplary words since it does appear in the natural flow of some diphthongs .

tone.says: Sec. 2.3.1: three basic tones - high level (55), mid level (33), low falling (21); the mid-level and low-falling tones each split into lax and tense subcategories (tense-vowel syllables), tense realisations slightly higher in pitch but written with the same numerals ('tense low falling tone of 21 is still marked as 21 although its actual pitch is slightly higher'); a high falling 51 is marked only in some words where it arises from diphthong contraction (e.g. tsha55a21tse33 'these'); Table 2-4…

sources.note: Abstract only (CQVIP): instrumental study of monosyllabic and disyllabic tones of Mingzudan village, Longtan township, Yuanjiang County: '山苏彝语明祖单话有5个调:高平调55,次高调44,中平调33,中/低降调31/21和低升调223/224。其中,低升调主要出现在汉语借词中,双音节无连读变调情况' (five tones; low rising only in Chinese loans; no tone sandhi in disyllables).
